newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia formally announces election results.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia formally announces election results.

text.p: Indonesia formally announced the results of the May 29 general elections on Monday, saying the ruling Golkar party had won 325 seats in the 500-member parliament.
The country's Election Institute said the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) won 89 seats, while the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) won 11.
The other 75 seats in the assembly are reserved for the military, which does not vote.
The PDI, badly split after former party chief Megawati Sukarnoputri was ousted from her post last year, thus gains the minimum number of seats required under parliamentary regulations.
The legislature has 11 commissions and the three parties are required to be represented on each of them.

Last week, politicians said the PDI may fall short of the required 11 seats and there were appeals to the other two parties to transfer some of their votes to the PDI to avoid a constitutional crisis. However, the PPP rejected the porposal.
